329612.title: The lower-bound conjecture for coefficients of Ehrhart polynomials
329612.statement:
Let ${\mathcal P} \subset {\mathbb R}^d$ be a lattice polytope with $d \geq 3$. Write $g_r({\mathcal P})$ for the coefficients of its Ehrhart polynomial, let $\operatorname{vol}({\mathcal P})$ denote its volume, and define

$$
N_{r,d}=\min\left\{C^d_{r,i}:\left\lceil\frac{d-1}{2}\right\rceil\leq i\leq d-2\right\}.
$$

Here $\operatorname{stirl}(d+1,r+1)$ denotes the Stirling-number term appearing in the Ehrhart-coefficient formula. **Lower-bound conjecture.** For every $r=1,\ldots,d-2$,

$$
g_r({\mathcal P})\geq \frac{1}{d!}\left((-1)^{d-r}\operatorname{stirl}(d+1,r+1)+(d!\operatorname{vol}({\mathcal P})-1)N_{r,d}\right),
$$

and these bounds are best possible for every volume. The conjecture extends the cases already proved for $r\in\{1,2,3,d-3,d-2\}$ or even $d-r$, and seeks the best possible lower bounds for the intermediate Ehrhart coefficients.

329771.title: The non-constant-boundary enumeration conjecture for tree $sl_n$ webs
329771.statement:
Let $R_{p,r}(k)$ denote the generalized Catalan number associated with parameters $p,r,k$. For $n \geq 3$, let an $sl_n$ web have a boundary string consisting of one boundary edge labelled $j$ followed by boundary edges labelled $1$; a web **lacks an internal cycle** when its underlying graph has no cycle away from the boundary. **Non-constant-boundary enumeration conjecture.** For any $n \geq 3$ and any $1 \leq j \leq n-1$, $(n-2)^k R_{n-1,n-j}(k)$ equals the number of connected $sl_n$ webs that lack an internal cycle and have a boundary string consisting of one $j$ followed by $nk + n - j$ consecutive 1's.
This is intended to generalize the preceding proposition for $sl_3$ webs with a non-constant boundary string. If true, it would give a combinatorial interpretation of $R_{p,r}(k)$ for all $k \geq 0$ whenever $1 \leq r \leq p-2$; the supplied text indicates that the result remains unproved.

332427.title: Local evacuation-shuffle algorithm for arbitrary skew tableaux
332427.statement:
Let $T$ be any (semi)standard skew tableau and let $mathbox$ be an inner co-corner of $T$. **Local evacuation-shuffle algorithm conjecture.** There exists a local algorithm for computing $mathe sh(mathbox,T)$ without rectifying $T$ such that:

1. Each step exchanges $mathbox$ with an entry of $T$ of weakly increasing value.
2. The slide-equivalence class of $T$ is preserved throughout the algorithm.
3. The algorithm specializes to jeu de taquin when $T$ has straight shape and to $math{local\text{-}esh}$ when $T$ is ballot.

Each step should correspond, by conjugating with rectification, to a jeu de taquin slide of $mathbox$ through the rectification of $(mathbox,T)$. This proposes a uniform local description of evacuation-shuffle beyond the ballot and straight-shape cases; the existence of such an algorithm for arbitrary (semi)standard skew tableaux remains open.

332857.title: Duality conjecture for all pages of the local Hodge–de Rham spectral sequences
332857.statement:
Let $A$ be a complete local ring with coefficient field $k$ of characteristic zero, and let $R$ be as in the construction of the local Hodge–de Rham homology and cohomology spectral sequences. Write their pages as $E_r^{p,q}$ and $\tilde{E}_r^{p,q}$, respectively, let $n=\dim R$, and let $V^{\vee}$ denote the $k$-linear dual of a $k$-vector space $V$. **Duality conjecture.** Beginning with the $E_2$-terms, the homology and cohomology spectral sequences are $k$-dual to each other: for every $r\geq 2$ and all $p,q$, 
$$
E_r^{n-p,n-q}\simeq (\tilde{E}_r^{p,q})^{\vee},
$$
 and the differentials are likewise dual. This conjecture restates the earlier expectation in a precise form. The duality at the $E_2$-page is proved in the paper, while duality for all later pages and differentials remains open.

333345.title: Vanishing-boundary conjecture for configuration spaces of one-connected graphs
333345.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a graph consisting of two arbitrary graphs connected by a single edge, and let $D_n(\Gamma)$ denote the configuration space of $n$ indistinguishable particles on $\Gamma$. In the Mayer–Vietoris decomposition, let $X_k$ be any subcomplex, with boundary map

$$
\delta:H_m(X_k)\longrightarrow H_{m-1}(A_k\cap B_k),\qquad m\geq 2.
$$

**Vanishing-boundary conjecture.** For indistinguishable particles on one-connected graphs from this class, the map $\delta$ always has trivial image:

$$
\operatorname{im}\delta=0.
$$

The conjecture would eliminate the obstruction coming from the Mayer–Vietoris boundary map and imply, in the relevant degree, that $H_2(X_k)\cong\operatorname{coker}\Phi_k$ and $\operatorname{ker}\Phi_k=0$. The paper reports no numerical evidence of counterexamples in the stated class, while noting that nontrivial images occur for other examples, including distinguishable particles on tree graphs.

333657.title: Multivariate alternating-sum partition identity for modulus m
333657.statement:
Let $m\geq 2$. For a partition $\lambda$, let $\Sigma_i(\lambda)$ denote the $i$th component of its alternating sum type, and let $l_i(\mu)$ denote the number of parts of $\mu$ congruent to $i$ modulo $m$. Let $P$ be the set of partitions in which each part is repeated at most $m-1$ times, and let $Q$ be the set of partitions with no parts congruent to $0$ modulo $m$. **The alternating-sum partition conjecture.** The multivariate generating functions satisfy

$$
\sum_{\lambda \in P} z_{1}^{\Sigma_{1}(\lambda)} z_{2}^{\Sigma_{2}(\lambda) } \dots z_{m-1} ^{\Sigma_{m-1}(\lambda) } q^{|\lambda |} = \sum_{\mu \in Q} z_{1}^{l_{1}(\mu)} z_{2}^{l_{2}(\mu) } \dots z_{m-1} ^{l_{m-1}(\mu) } q^{|\mu |}.
$$

Equivalently, for every $n$ and every alternating sum type $(\Sigma_{1},\Sigma_{2},\dots,\Sigma_{m-1})$, the number of partitions of $n$ with that alternating sum type equals the number of partitions of $n$ having $\Sigma_i$ parts congruent to $i$ modulo $m$ for each $1\leq i\leq m-1$. This conjecture seeks a refinement of Euler's partition theorem and its modulus-$m$ companions by matching alternating-sum statistics with residue-class statistics; its status is not resolved in the supplied source.

333997.title: Centered-set conjecture for k-chains in grid posets
333997.statement:
Let $[m]^d$ be the product poset, ordered coordinatewise: $\mathbf{a}\leq\mathbf{b}$ when $a_i\leq b_i$ for every $i\in[d]$. A $k$-chain is a set of $k$ distinct points satisfying $\mathbf{a}_1\leq\cdots\leq\mathbf{a}_k$. For $\mathcal{F}\subseteq[m]^d$, call $\mathcal{F}$ **$m$-centered** if, whenever $\mathbf{a}\in\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathbf{b}\notin\mathcal{F}$,

$$
\left\lvert\sum_{i=1}^d a_i-\frac{dm}{2}\right\rvert\leq\left\lvert\sum_{i=1}^d b_i-\frac{dm}{2}\right\rvert,
$$

and equality implies $\sum_{i=1}^d a_i\geq\sum_{i=1}^d b_i$.

**Centered-set conjecture.** Given $m$, there exists a number $d_0(m)$ such that if $d\geq d_0(m)$, then the sets minimizing the number of $k$-chains among subsets of $[m]^d$ of any prescribed size are $m$-centered.

This is a proposed extension of Kleitman's question from the Boolean lattice to grid posets. The source emphasizes that the conjecture is a natural guess with little supporting evidence and does not claim uniqueness of the minimizers.

334392.title: Conjecture on the alternating or symmetric action of the Markoff automorphism group
334392.statement:
Let $H(p)$ be the permutation group induced by the action of $\operatorname{Out}(\mathbf{F}_{2})$ on $\mathbb{Y}_{-2}(\mathbb{F}_{p})$, and let

$$
n=|\mathbb{Y}_{-2}(\mathbb{F}_{p})|.
$$

Here $\mathbb{Y}_{-2}(\mathbb{F}_{p})$ is the set of $N$-orbits in $\mathbb{X}_{-2}^{*}(\mathbb{F}_{p})$, where $N$ is the Klein four-group of even sign changes. **Alternating-group conjecture.** For every prime $p>3$, $H(p)$ is the full alternating group or the full symmetric group according to the congruence class of $p$ modulo $16$; specifically, the preceding theorem shows that $H(p)\leq A_n$ exactly when $p\equiv3\pmod{16}$, and the conjecture asserts the corresponding complete determination of $H(p)$. This conjecture is motivated by computations for $p\leq47$ and by the transitive action of $\operatorname{Out}(\mathbf{F}_{2})$ on the relevant Markoff surface orbits; the exact group identification beyond the parity criterion remains open.

336115.title: The coloop-extension conjecture for powerful sets
336115.statement:
Let $T\subseteq\mathbb{F}_2^n$ be a powerful set, meaning that for every subset of coordinates, the number of vectors in $T$ that are zero on those coordinates is a power of $2$. A vector has **weight** $1$ if exactly one of its coordinates is nonzero. A **coloop extension** of a set is obtained by adjoining a new coordinate so that each vector of a set $S$ occurs with both possible values in that coordinate.

**Coloop-extension conjecture.** If $T$ is a powerful set with at least one vector of weight $1$, then $T$ is a coloop extension of some powerful set $S$.

The preceding observation shows that every coloop extension of a powerful set has a vector of weight $1$; the conjecture asserts the converse. The supplied text does not indicate whether this converse has been proved or disproved.

336579.title: Aharoni–Howard–Huang–Loh–Sudakov rainbow matching conjecture
336579.statement:
A $t$-matching is a $k$-uniform hypergraph consisting of $t$ pairwise disjoint edges. Families $\mathcal{F}_1,\ldots,\mathcal{F}_t\subseteq\binom{[n]}{k}$ are **cross free** of an ordered $t$-matching if there is no ordered $t$-matching $(E_1,\ldots,E_t)$ with $E_i\in\mathcal{F}_i$ for every $i$. Let $k\le\frac{t-1}{t}n$. **Aharoni–Howard–Huang–Loh–Sudakov rainbow matching conjecture.**

$$
\min\{|\mathcal{F}_1|,\ldots,|\mathcal{F}_t|\}\le\binom{n}{k}-\binom{n-t+1}{k}.
$$

Equality is attained if all the families $\mathcal{F}_1,\ldots,\mathcal{F}_t$ are equal to the same $(t-1,1)$-star. The conjecture is described as a strengthening of the Erdős matching conjecture and was raised independently by Aharoni and Howard and by Huang, Loh, and Sudakov. Its resolution status is not specified here.

336752.title: The wreath-product quotient conjecture for triangle groups
336752.statement:
Let $G=\Delta(p,q,r)$ be the triangle group with presentation

$$
\Delta(p,q,r)=\langle x,y\mid x^p=y^q=(xy)^r=1\rangle.
$$

Assume that $p$ is prime and $p\leq q\leq r$, and choose an integer $m$ such that the alternating group ${\cal A}_m$ can be generated by two $p$-cycles. Let ${\cal A}_{\mathrm{deg}}$ be the alternating group on $\mathrm{deg}$ letters and ${\cal A}_m\wr {\cal A}_{\mathrm{deg}}$ the corresponding wreath product. **Wreath-product quotient conjecture.** For all but finitely many integers $\mathrm{deg}$, $G$ maps onto

$$
{\cal A}_m\wr {\cal A}_{\mathrm{deg}}.
$$

This conjecture extends the preceding quotient construction from the semidirect product $C_p^{\mathrm{deg}-1}\rtimes {\cal A}_{\mathrm{deg}}$ to wreath products. The source does not state whether the conjecture has been resolved.

337040.title: Finiteness and strict growth conjecture for compact packings with n radii
337040.statement: For each $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\Pi_n$ denote the set of compact packings of the plane with $n$ distinct circle radii, represented by radius ratios $(r_{n-1},r_{n-2},\ldots,r_1)$. The construction obtained by filling interstitial gaps of a compact $(n-1)$-packing corresponds to the truncation $(r_{n-2},\ldots,r_1)\in\Pi_{n-1}$. **Finiteness and strict growth conjecture.** For every $n\in\mathbb{N}$, the set $\Pi_n$ is finite and the sequence $(|\Pi_n|)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ is strictly increasing. Furthermore, for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$, there exists an element $(r_{n-1},r_{n-2},\ldots,r_1)\in\Pi_n$ with $(r_{n-2},\ldots,r_1)\notin\Pi_{n-1}$; equivalently, not every compact $n$-packing arises from filling interstitial gaps of a compact $(n-1)$-packing. The conjecture extends the observed finiteness of $\Pi_2$ and $\Pi_3$ and predicts genuinely new compact packings at every number of radii, rather than only those obtained by recursively filling gaps.

337062.title: Uniform edge betweenness centrality in seven circulant graph classes
337062.statement:
A **circulant graph** $C_m(a_1,a_2,a_3)$ has vertex set indexed modulo $m$ and edges generated by the listed steps. The following seven parameterized classes are proposed:

$$
C_{20+8(n-1)}(1,2n+2,2n+4),\quad n=1,2,3,\dots
$$

$$
C_{32+8(n-1)}(1,2n+5,2n+7),\quad n=1,2,3,\dots
$$

$$
C_{20+16(n-1)}(1,4n,8n+1),\quad n=1,2,3,\dots
$$

$$
C_{28+16(n-1)}(1,4n+4,8n+5),\quad n=1,2,3,\dots
$$

$$
C_{32+8(n-1)}(1,2n+5,4n+11),\quad n=1,2,3,\dots
$$

$$
C_{32+8(n-1)}(1,2n+7,4n+11),\quad n=1,2,3,\dots
$$

$$
C_{49+14(n-1)}(1,2n+6,4n+9),\quad n=1,2,3,\dots
$$

**Uniform edge betweenness centrality conjecture.** Each of these seven classes of circulant graphs has uniform edge betweenness centrality but is not edge-transitive.

The authors identify these classes as further examples with the same unusual combination of properties as the proved class $C_{18n+3}(1,6n)$. The statement is posed as an open problem, so uniformity and non-edge-transitivity remain to be established for all indicated values of $n$.

337548.title: Rigidity Conjecture for generalized Ulam sets
337548.statement:
Let $U(a,N)$ be the generalized Ulam set with initial positive integers $a,N$. For a positive integer $L$, let $c$ range over the units $(\mathbb{Z}/L\mathbb{Z})^\times$. Let $A(x,y,s)$ denote the corresponding generalized interval component used in the decomposition, with integer parameters $m_{i_l},p_{i_l},k_{i_l},r_{i_l}$ and index parameter $s^{(l)}_{i_l}$.

**Rigidity Conjecture.** For every positive integer $a$, there exists an integer $L\geq1$ such that, for every $c\in(\mathbb{Z}/L\mathbb{Z})^\times$, there exists a positive integer $N_0\equiv c\pmod L$ such that for every $N\geq N_0$ satisfying $N\equiv c\pmod L$, one has a disjoint-union decomposition

$$
U(a,N)=\bigcup_{l=1}^{\infty}\bigsqcup_{i_l=1}^{\infty}A\left(m_{i_l}N+p_{i_l},k_{i_l}N+r_{i_l},s^{(l)}_{i_l}\right),
$$

with $m_{i_l}=k_{i_l}$ if and only if $l=1$. This conjecture proposes eventual, residue-class-dependent rigidity for generalized Ulam sets; the preceding discussion says that existing rigidity theorems only control initial segments, while numerical data suggests this stronger global structure.

337664.title: Finite-strategy conjecture for normal quasicones
337664.statement:
Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be an affine Kac–Moody algebra, let $V$ be a weight module, and let $\mathfrak{C}$ be the set of normal quasicones arising as annihilators of vectors in $V$. Let $\mathfrak{S}$ denote the set of strategies, where a strategy is a finite composition of root operators satisfying the stated nonvanishing, quasicone, and root-sum conditions. **Finite-strategy conjecture.** There is a finite set of strategies $\mathcal{S}\subset\mathfrak{S}$ such that the number of normal quasicones where no strategy succeeds is zero, namely

$$
\bigcap_{C\in\mathfrak{C}}\left\{\#\operatorname{Ann}(sv)\geq\#C\text{ for all }s\in\mathcal{S}\right\}=\emptyset.
$$

If true, this would ensure that every normal quasicone admits a successful strategy and support the proposed classification method. The supplied source gives no resolution status.

337922.title: Factorization and positivity conjecture for asymmetric quantum Rabi constraint polynomials
337922.statement:
For $N\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$, let $P^{(N,\varepsilon)}_k(x,y)$ denote the constraint-polynomial family defined by the recurrence in the source, and write $P^{(N,\varepsilon)}_N(x,y)$ for its constraint polynomial.

**Factorization and positivity conjecture.** For $\ell,N\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$, there exists a polynomial $A^\ell_N(x,y)\in\mathbb{Z}[x,y]$ such that

$$
P^{(N+\ell,-\ell/2)}_{N+\ell}(x,y)=A^\ell_N(x,y)P^{(N,\ell/2)}_N(x,y).
$$

Moreover, $A^\ell_N(x,y)$ is positive for every $x,y>0$.

This factorization would explain the relation between constraint polynomials at positive and negative half-integer bias and, together with positivity, transfer information about their positive roots. The surrounding text presents it as the main objective, but the supplied excerpt gives no resolution evidence.

340982.title: The potential-function conjecture for critical graphs
340982.statement:
Fix an integer $k\geq 6$. For a graph $G$, let

$$
T(G)=\max\{2a(H)+b(H):H\subseteq G\text{ is a union of vertex-disjoint cliques}\},
$$

where $a(H)$ is the number of components of $H$ isomorphic to $K_{k-1}$ and $b(H)$ is the number of components of $H$ isomorphic to $K_{k-2}$. For positive real numbers $\varepsilon$ and $\delta$, define the **$(\varepsilon,\delta)$-potential** by

$$
p(G)=((k-2)(k+1)+\varepsilon)|V(G)|-2(k-1)|E(G)|-\delta T(G).
$$

**Potential-function conjecture.** For every $k\geq 6$, there exist $\varepsilon_k,\delta_k,P_k>0$ such that the $(\varepsilon_k,\delta_k)$-potential satisfies

$$
p(K_k)=k(k-3)+k\varepsilon_k-2\delta_k,
$$

$\displaystyle p(G)\leq k(k-3)+|V(G)|\varepsilon_k-\left(2+\frac{|V(G)|-1}{k-1}\right)\delta_k$ if $G$ is $k$-Ore and $G\neq K_k$, and

$$
p(G)\leq k(k-3)-P_k
$$

if $G$ is $k$-critical and not $k$-Ore. Here a graph is $k$-critical if $\chi(G)=k$ and every proper subgraph has chromatic number less than $k$, and $k$-Ore graphs are the graphs obtained from $K_k$ by repeated Ore-compositions. This conjecture proposes a potential gap for non-$k$-Ore critical graphs while prescribing the potential of $K_k$ and bounding it on nontrivial $k$-Ore graphs; it is intended to provide the structural and discharging framework for the unresolved cases $6\leq k\leq 32$.

373107.title: Wedge-of-spheres conjecture for robust clique complexes of square-sequence graphs
373107.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with a square sequence

$$
C_4 \cong H_1 \subset H_2 \subset \cdots \subset H_n \cong G,
$$

where $n\geq 1$, and let $\mathsf{Cliq}_{k}(G)$ denote the $k$-robust clique complex of $G$.

**Wedge-of-spheres conjecture.** For all $k\geq 2$, the complex $\mathsf{Cliq}_{k}(G)$ is homotopy equivalent to a wedge sum of $(2k-3)$-dimensional spheres. Moreover, the number of spheres is determined by a recurrence relation based on the homotopy type of $\mathsf{Cliq}_{k}(H_{n-1})$ and the specific attachment of the $n$-th square.

This conjecture seeks to extend the established homotopy results for robust clique complexes from $k\in\{2,3\}$ to all $k\geq 2$. The stated recurrence is not given explicitly here, so determining the sphere count and proving the claimed wedge decomposition remain open.

381292.title: A stronger rainbow degree-sequence conjecture for bipartite graphs
381292.statement:
Let $F_i$, $i\leq k$, be subgraphs of $K_{n,n}$, and let $A=(a_{ij})$ be the $k\times n$ matrix whose entry $a_{ij}$ is the degree of $v_j$ in $F_i$. Let $r_i(A)$ be the sum of the $i$-th row, so that $r_i(A)=|F_i|$. For sequences, write $\overrightarrow{a}$ for the rearrangement of $a$ in non-decreasing order, and compare sequences componentwise after rearrangement. **Stronger rainbow degree-sequence conjecture.** If

$$
\sum_{i\leq j}\overrightarrow{r}_i>j(j-1)n
$$

for every $j\leq k$, then there exists a permutation $\pi:[k]\to[k]$ such that

$$
\sum_{i\leq j}\overrightarrow{a}_{i\pi(i)}>j(j-1)
$$

for every $j$. This strengthens the preceding theorem by requiring simultaneous inequalities for the rearranged selected columns, rather than only the componentwise lower bound represented by $(1,2,\ldots,k)$.

382416.title: Eigenvalue bound conjecture for covariance matrices of volume power functionals
382416.statement:
Let $\Sigma_n$ be the covariance matrix associated with the volume power functional in the critical regime. Assume that, for every $m\in\{0,\ldots,k_n\}$, the matrices $A_m^{>1}$ satisfy Requirement 1, and let $S_m$ be the corresponding bound. Denote the eigenvalues of $\Sigma_n$ by

$$
\lambda_1^{\Sigma_n}\leq\cdots\leq\lambda_n^{\Sigma_n}.
$$

**Eigenvalue bound conjecture.** These eigenvalues satisfy

$$
0\leq\lambda_1^{\Sigma_n}\leq\cdots\leq\lambda_n^{\Sigma_n}\leq (k_n+1)\max_{m=0,\ldots,k_n}S_m\left(\sum_{i=1}^n\frac{1}{a_{i,m}^2}\right).
$$

The bound is proposed for the covariance matrix in the critical regime and follows the preceding spectral estimates for the matrices $A_m^{>1}$, subject to the stated requirement. Its resolution would provide a uniform control on the eigenvalues of $\Sigma_n$ in terms of the quantities $S_m$ and $a_{i,m}$; the supplied text gives no evidence that it has been proved or refuted.
